key_terms.meaning: A condition–action statement that turns sensor values into actuator commands, run locally or in the cloud.
A device that changes the physical world, such as a relay, motor, valve or lock.
A local device that bridges short-range sensors to the internet and can keep rules running during an outage.
A saved rule set that keeps basic control working when the cloud link is down.
A sensor, often magnetic or radar, that reports whether a bay is free or occupied.
Low-power wide-area network: long-range radio for small, infrequent messages from battery devices.
A cellular LPWAN standard for narrowband devices on licensed operator spectrum.
A message that links a bay, vehicle session and charge so the operator can bill the user.
Industrial Internet of Things: connected machines and systems that use production data for control, maintenance and planning.
An industrial communication standard for secure, typed data exchange between machines and business systems.
A software model of a machine or process kept current by sensor data and used for prediction.
Continuous or periodic sensing of machine health signals to catch faults before failure.
Computation joined to a physical process in a closed loop, where timing and sensing affect the physical result.
A cycle where sensed output changes the control action, which changes the output again.
Variation in message delay from one sample to the next.
Sensing a distant process, sending data through a gateway to a service, and alerting a person or controller.
Measured data sent from a remote site to a monitoring centre.
A limit on a measured value that triggers an alert when crossed.
Farming that uses local sensor and weather data to apply water, fertiliser or pesticide only where needed.
A temperature-controlled logistics chain monitored from farm or factory to retail.

takeaways: A smart home works well when basic rules keep running locally and the cloud adds visibility, not dependence.
Smart parking shows the full chain: sensor, low-power radio, operator cloud, payment and user app.
IIoT is not just sensors on machines; it joins production data to maintenance, control and planning systems.
A cyber-physical system fails physically when sampling delay, network jitter or sensor error is ignored.
Remote monitoring needs clear alarm thresholds, acknowledged alerts and a safe fallback action.
Domain case studies are judged by power, connectivity, cost, environment and user constraints, not by the sensor list.
Edge computing helps when the loop needs low delay or the link is expensive, but it adds devices to manage.
Security, privacy and maintenance decide whether a deployment survives after the pilot.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask you to trace a full application chain—sensor, network, cloud rule, actuator or user—and justify protocol and deployment choices for a named domain.

bank.q: Explain the chain from a sensor event to an actuator action in a smart home. Include where local and cloud rules sit and what happens when the internet link fails.
outline: sensor event is captured and normalised
rule engine evaluates condition–action statements
local controller versus cloud service placement
actuator command and user notification
fallback keeps basic control during an outage

bank.q: Describe how a smart parking system detects occupancy, sends the message over a low-power wide-area network, and completes payment.
outline: bay sensor detects vehicle presence
node sends a small occupancy message
LPWAN gateway or operator cloud maps the bay and session
payment app or wallet completes the charge
battery, radio coverage and vehicle-data privacy are limits

bank.q: Define IIoT and explain how it differs from consumer IoT in device ruggedness, latency needs and business-system integration.
outline: IIoT connects machines and business systems
devices are rugged, long-life and often fixed
control and safety need bounded latency
data goes to historians, MES and ERP
example: pump-motor condition monitoring

bank.q: Explain a cyber-physical system with a closed feedback loop. Use one example and show how sensing and timing enter the physical result.
outline: computation and physical plant are joined
sensors, controller and actuators form the loop
closed loop changes action from measured output
example: cruise control or robot arm
delay and sensing error become physical error

bank.q: Design a remote water-level monitoring and pump-control system for a village tank. Choose sensor, gateway, cloud alarm and safe fallback, and state the main constraints.
outline: level sensor and pump relay or contactor
gateway with local threshold and hysteresis
cloud dashboard plus SMS or app alarm
manual override and dry-run protection
power, connectivity and maintenance constraints

bank.q: Apply a smart home rule engine to a flat in a city with frequent power cuts. Describe local control, cloud alerts and the safe state during an outage.
outline: door, motion and temperature sensors
local controller keeps lights and security running
cloud sends remote alerts and schedules
battery backup and cellular fallback
user override and event log

bank.q: A city has 200 parking bays and must report occupancy and collect payment. Compare NB-IoT and LoRaWAN for the radio link and recommend one with reasons.
outline: NB-IoT uses licensed operator spectrum and SIM management
LoRaWAN can be private but has duty-cycle limits
message size and reporting rate fit both for occupancy
payment needs reliable backhaul and secure session records
choose by coverage, ownership, cost and maintenance

bank.q: Apply IIoT condition monitoring to a plant pump motor. Show the path from vibration and temperature data to a maintenance action.
outline: vibration, temperature and current sensors
edge feature extraction reduces data
cloud trend and threshold alarm
maintenance ticket in the plant system
baseline and false-alarm handling

bank.q: Design an agriculture IoT case study with soil-moisture sensing, valve control and farmer alerts. State how you would judge whether it is a good deployment.
outline: soil-moisture nodes and valve controller
gateway and farmer SMS or app alert
schedule, manual override and dry-run protection
power, water pressure and connectivity constraints
judge by water saved, reliability and cost

bank.q: Analyze how sampling delay, network jitter and sensor error in a cyber-physical control loop change the physical result. Use a robot arm or drone example.
outline: sampling delay shifts the measured state
jitter makes control intervals uneven
actuator lag adds overshoot or oscillation
sensor error and calibration offset the result
mitigate with edge control, timestamps and watchdog

bank.q: Evaluate a smart-city deployment that adds street lighting, waste-bin sensing and smart parking. Discuss shared network, power, privacy, maintenance and cost per service.
outline: each service has different message rate and power need
shared network can reduce cost but raises failure impact
cameras and payment create privacy duties
maintenance and interoperability decide uptime
judge by reliability and cost per service, not device count

bank.q: Evaluate security and privacy risks in a remote e-health monitoring service. Propose safeguards across device, gateway, cloud and clinician alerting.
outline: health data is sensitive and needs consent
device theft and insecure gateway are entry points
use encryption, authentication and data minimisation
alarm acknowledgement and clinician escalation
audit logs and privacy rules

bank.q: Compare an agriculture irrigation case study with a logistics cold-chain case study. Judge both by constraints such as power, connectivity, cost, environment and user action.
outline: agriculture constraints: power, water, rural link
cold chain constraints: temperature, motion, handover
compare sensors, network, cloud rule and user
compare failure modes and cost
judge by constraints and outcomes, not sensor list

glossary.def: A device that converts a control signal into physical action, such as a relay, motor or valve.
A device that connects local sensors to a wider network and may run local rules.
Software that evaluates condition–action rules and triggers actions when conditions are met.
A home where sensors, rules and actuators automate lighting, security, comfort or energy use.
A parking system that senses bay occupancy, guides drivers and often handles payment.
A low-power wide-area network designed for long-range, small, infrequent messages from battery devices.
A narrowband cellular LPWAN standard used on licensed mobile-operator spectrum.
An open LPWAN protocol that uses LoRa radio and can be deployed as a private network.
A lightweight publish–subscribe messaging protocol often used between IoT devices and cloud services.
An industrial standard for secure, typed and interoperable data exchange between machines and systems.
A software model of a physical asset kept current by data and used for monitoring or prediction.
The use of connected data, automation and analytics to make production more flexible and responsive.
Industrial Internet of Things: connected industrial machines and systems that share data for control, maintenance and planning.
A system where computation controls a physical process through a closed loop of sensing and actuation.
A control cycle in which measured output changes the control action and therefore the output.
Variation in delay between successive messages or samples.
The time taken for data or a control action to travel from source to destination.
Sensing a distant process and sending data to a service that informs or alerts a person.
Measured data sent automatically from a remote site to a monitoring centre.
A value limit that triggers an alert when a measurement crosses it.
Processing data near the sensors or machine instead of sending everything to the cloud.
Farming that uses local data to apply water, fertiliser or pesticide only where it is needed.
A temperature-controlled supply chain monitored from production to retail.
A utility meter that records consumption and sends readings or events to the operator.
